rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT-LDA calculation with a well-known functional (LDA-PZ) and basis set (DZP/SZ), applied to Si quantum dots. No custom method; simply using off-the-shelf software with documented parameters. Some domain knowledge needed for input setup, but no research-grade novelty.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: compile/set up OpenMX, build crystal-derived cluster models with passivation, run geometry optimizations (BFGS) for at least three QD sizes, perform SCF calculations, extract HOMO-LUMO gaps, and apply a constant correction. This involves multiple DFT tasks with dependency (relaxed structures needed for SCF) and careful data extraction. Not trivial but still a common computational chemistry workflow.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT-LDA using the established OpenMX package to compute size-dependent gaps of small Si quantum dots. There is no novel algorithm or mathematical derivation; the method is a conventional computational materials science workflow. Execution involves installing OpenMX, constructing structures, running several DFT calculations (bulk and ~14 QDs), and extracting gaps. The pipeline is moderate but well-understood. Resource requirements are minimal (CPU-only, small clusters).

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT on silicon clusters with up to ~300 atoms using localized numerical atomic orbitals (LCAO). The calculations are CPU-only, lightweight (few GB RAM, no large datasets), and run on a single workstation.
